newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Goldman Sachs unveils new EMU sentiment indicator.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs unveils new EMU sentiment indicator.

text.p: Market expectations about Europe's planned single currency starting on schedule can be gauged by comparing the Ecu's spot value against the value of the Ecu basket, according to a new study by Goldman Sachs.
"When the value of the Ecu declines relative to the basket Ecu, sentiment towards EMU is deteriorating and vice versa," said Martin Brookes, author of the report.

Under the transition plan for monetary union, the basket Ecu -- defined by a fixed weighting of 11 currencies -- will convert into the euro at a rate of one for one and Ecu assets will be converted at a similar rate in euro assets.
The study argues that if financial markets are absolutely confident that EMU will begin on time, the forward value of the Ecu for January 1, 1999 should be equal to its basket value.
"The probability of EMU priced into markets can be calculated from the forward values of the Ecu and the basket Ecu," the study said.

Since the beginning of the year the probability that EMU will happen as planned has averaged 75 percent, dipping to 60 percent after the French election at the beginning of June and then to just above 50 percent on June 10.
During the second half of June the probability index rose and is now over 80 percent, the report said.
Goldman Sachs said they will publish the results of the index on a weekly basis so that investors can monitor changing sentiment towards EMU.
